identity.title: Polynomial-Delay MAG Listing with Novel Locally Complete Orientation Rules

problem.claim: Given a partial ancestral graph representing a MAG Markov equivalence class, list all MAGs for downstream causal tasks.

gap.claim: Existing orientation rules, including the proposed rules, are not complete for incorporating general background knowledge; this motivates additional rules.

contributions.claim: A MAG-listing method using recursively introduced singleton background knowledge and sound, locally complete orientation rules.
A polynomial-delay procedure that outputs all and only MAGs in the equivalence class under the proposed process.
Two counterexamples for general background knowledge, motivating two additional rules.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present what they describe as the first polynomial-delay MAG-listing method, enabled by enumerated singleton background knowledge and novel orientation rules.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their procedure outputs all and only MAGs in the MEC with polynomial delay.
The authors report experimental results validating the efficiency of the proposed MAG-listing method.
The authors report two counterexamples showing that existing rules, including theirs, are not yet complete for general background knowledge.

narrative_sequence.summary: MAGs characterize causal relations among observables when latent variables may be present.
Observational data generally identifies only a partial graph and leaves causal relations uncertain, making MAG listing useful for downstream tasks.
The paper introduces singleton background knowledge together with sound and locally complete orientation rules, recursively applying them for listing.
For general background knowledge, counterexamples reveal incompleteness and motivate two further rules; experiments report efficiency.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates the polynomial-delay result for singleton background knowledge from the incompleteness issue for general background knowledge.

lessons.interpretation: Explicitly scoping a guarantee can make its applicability and remaining limitations easier to assess.
lessons.application: State the knowledge regime attached to each algorithmic guarantee, then separately identify broader regimes where completeness remains unresolved.
lessons.exception: This separation is less useful when the method and guarantee genuinely cover the same unrestricted regime.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the polynomial bound, input-size dependence, datasets, baselines, or quantitative efficiency results.
The exact definitions of singleton background knowledge, local completeness, and the two additional rules are not provided.
